In this study, a commercial Mg –6Zn–0.5Zr (ZK60) alloy was subjected to a low-temperature indirect extrusion process for grain reﬁnement and the tensile properties of the ﬁne-grained alloy at 250 °C were investigated.

This is ascribed to a combination of the initial dissolution of the pre-existing precipitates around grain boundaries during the superplastic deformation and subsequent heterogeneous precipitation at the grain boundaries upon cooling, suggestive of the activation of a local diffusional process, such as GBS, in the high-strain-rate superplastic ZK60 alloy.
In this study, a commercial Mg –6Zn–0.5Zr (ZK60) alloy was subjected to a low-temperature indirect extrusion process for grain reﬁnement
A cylindrical extrusion billet was prepared by induction melting in a graphite crucible under an inert atmosphere
The cast billet was homogenized at 440 °C for 4 h, followed by water quenching.
An indirect extrusion experiment was implemented at an initial billet temperature of 250 °C, a ram speed of 1.3 mm s−1, and an extrusion ratio of 25.
Fig. 1 b provides an EBSD orientation map of the ZK60 alloy processed by low-temperature indirect extrusion utilizing artiﬁcial cooling.
